correctness.summary: A projected-coordinate determinant formula, two diameter-induced transverse constraints, and a weighted complete-graph Laplacian reduce the problem to a sharp trace-determinant inequality. Equality conditions force and are attained by the unique simplex with the distinguished edge s and every other edge D.

limitations: The stability law controls edge lengths rather than Hausdorff, Banach-Mazur, altitude, inradius, or circumradius distance.
Only one prescribed edge is optimized explicitly; multiple simultaneous short-edge constraints are not treated.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; an equivalent older distance-geometry or folklore formulation may exist.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical largest-small-polytope results, recent aggregate edge-frame inequalities, special short/long-edge simplex constructions, and searches under prescribed/shortest-edge and edge-ratio terminology were checked. No located source gives the exact one-edge-conditioned volume profile, equality family, or inverse shortest-edge law.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The theorem refines the regular-simplex diameter extremum into a sharp all-scales stability profile and yields an explicit best-possible inverse bound on every edge from normalized volume.
